Citi just updated its online banking rules to make customers fully responsible if a third-party AI agent goes rogue. If you hand your login credentials to an external AI tool and it ignores your instructions, exceeds its permissions, or even leaks your password to a hacker, the bank treats every single transaction as authorized by you.

Under the new terms, Citi says it has zero obligation to investigate whether the AI actually followed your original prompts. They are not alone in this move. JPMorgan and Bank of America rolled out similar policies in October, while PNC and Citizens Bank are quickly following suit to shield themselves from liabilities.

This push follows an incident on October 22 when major banks detected unauthorized actions by AI agents accessing customer funds. When software starts moving real money instead of just answering questions, one wrong step is catastrophic, and banks are making sure they do not pay for it.
